When a Pokemon evolves, it assumes its new form within seconds. How is this biologically possible? Shouldn't it be a gradual evolution from one form to the next?

Fairly certain Pokemon abilities are not considered magic.

You know how mass is really just tightly packed energy? Through battling, pokemon absorb energy from around them, until they hit a peak where the current body cannot contain all of the energy it has absorbed. So a pokemon will then convert its mass back into energy, rearrange itself and expand to make room for the absorbed energy, then convert all of it back into mass to form the newly evolved pokemon.

Come to think of it, that's actually what the evolution animations in the games seem to show. They start glowing white, they become formless is some games (I think it was just Black and White), and then there's a blinding flash and voila, you've got an evolved Pokemon!

This seems to be the most likely hypothesis, though it's difficult to test these things. Pokemon seem to also fuel most of their attacks with this energy, so one has to assume that it has a finite supply that is constantly growing as the Pokemon progresses.
